lines: The sorcerer's golem approached with heavy footfalls.
The moment Kirara-senpai sharply swung her hand down, the golem suddenly stopped dead in its tracks.
Looking down at the giant's metal feet, kunai made of ice could be seen pinning them to the ground.
I had never seen that Jutsu before. And I gazed in awe at the speed of the attack.
It seemed that Kirara-senpai had devised a new technique to create kunai of ice from the moisture in the air.
She must have integrated the more rapid charge of cold air into her tactics after the battle with Euryale.
However, that level of restraint against that golem was hardlyー
As I'd feared, the golem broke the restraints of ice with force and tried to lunge at Kirara-senpai.
The cold air charged in Kirara-senpai's right arm was unleashed all at once.
Her ice claw instantly froze the golem, creating an ice statue that was even harder than the hardest mineral.
Apparently, the ice kunai were just a diversion to buy time to fully charge the cold air.
She seemed to have come up with that tactic so she could take enemies all on her own, which was very typical of her.
Alriiight! The big oaf is down! Those ghouls are nextーhuuuh!?
Kirara-senpai, who had just beautifully defeated the golem and was about to start on the ghouls, stood there flabbergasted.
With each gunshot that reverberated through the area, the ghouls were being obliterated one by one.
Ahahahahaha! This is perfect for a warm-up!!!
Both her quick-draw skills and the firepower of her weapon were nothing short of fierce.
One shot, one kill. She was taking down the ghouls with precision. Or rather, she was blowing them to pieces.
Her gun, which she called the Jet Revolver, didn't appear to be a regular handgun. Perhaps the rounds weren't, either.
They could probably blow away not just those ghouls, but even ogres like they were nothing.
Hey!! Stop shooting all of them! You're stealing my kills!!
First come, first served! And my guns are finally warmed up! Take this, and this, and this, and this!!
I couldn't even tell when she reloaded.
As if it were a shooting game or something, the ghouls were blown away one after another.
Ahh, dammit!! I can't even get a full charge off! Hraaaaaaaaaaaaagh!!
Kirara-senpai also leapt into the fray and began to wield her ice fists, freezing and smashing the ghouls to bits.
This isn't the time to be impressed, Shikanosuke-chan! Let's show them what heberybody can do!
Hebiko and Shikanosuke weren't about to sit this one out either.
They were no match for Annreed and Kirara-senpai, but they were slowly yet surely taking out the monsters.
Sheesh. I guess commands aren't needed...
All I could do was stay in total spectator mode.
But I wasn't as bad as the other one at least.
Tell me when this is over.
Neither intending to fight nor watch, Chevalier had sat down on some of the rubble and begun to read a book.

Thanks to a great showing from two, some fine effort from the other two, and no help at all from the final two members, the battle at the ruins finally ended. And finally, we arrived at our destination which was the church.
Shikanosuke was even more scared than usual, and Hebiko was timidly glancing around her surroundings as well.
The sorcerer's lair is in the basement of this church. Hm-hm, I can't wait to see what's inside.
Huh, it looks just like I expected. It's perfect for a gloomy sorcerer.
Annreed and Kirara-senpai, on the other hand, were in high spirits for the real battle that lay ahead.
Chevalier wonders what kind of magic they'll use to welcome her. Hopefully nothing banal.
Perhaps Chevalier was also excited about what awaited us, as she suddenly shut the book she'd been reading all along with a slam.
When I opened the unpleasant-sounding door and entered the church...
The candles on the altar lit up by themselves.
Shikanosuke burst into tears and clung to me.
Even Hebiko screamed and, for some reason, wrapped her tentacles around me, squeezing tightly.
Gh-gh-gh... T-, too tight... You... morons... L-, lemme go...
I could feel the life being crushed out of me...
This was it. This was the end...
But suddenly there was... a chill?
Hebiko's tentacles relinquished me, and Shikanosuke also jumped away in surprise.
I seemed to owe Kirara-senpai for giving those two a quick cooldown.
Phew... I'm alive! You two could've killed me, you know?
S-, sorry. I didn't mean to.
What's the big deal even!? Oni are scarier than ghosts, you know!
Kirara-senpai was looking like she was pretty fed up with our antics.
She had made me worry in Tokyo Kingdom's downtown, but she was as reliable as could be when the situation called for it.
She also seemed completely unfazed by the idea of ghosts.
Come to think of it, Oni and ghosts could almost be considered to be related. Although Kirara-senpai would definitely be angry if she heard thatーwhat with the blood of the Oni running in her veins.
Oh, those aren't ghosts. Some magic was activated since the seal was broken.
Who'd break something like that? What a nuisance.
You mean, these magical things are pouring out because the refugees broke down the basement wall along with the seal on this sorcerer's lair?
Not the most precise way of putting it, but not a bad way to imagine it either.
And we're not even inside yet. This is getting very interesting.
Annreed whistled to herself, excited for what was to come.
That this lair's master is one tough customer, Captain.
The time Kirara-senpai and I confronted the witch Euryale inadvertently came to my mind.
My luck when it came to dealing with magic was just the worst...
Kirara-senpai also didn't appear to have forgotten about the witch. It didn't seem to be affecting her in the slightest, however.
They're pretty cocky for a sorcerer, aren't they? Next time they're gonna have to answer these frozen fists!
She grumbled on like she was a bully in some cartoon about a robo-cat.
There's no turning back now, Captain.
Not like we would anyway. Let's go.
Urrgh, I've got a bad feeling about this.
Hebiko hopes there won't be any ghosts or anything...
Chevalier wonders what awaits us, ufufu.
With such trepidations in mind, we headed down into the church's basement.
